question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-593 (Session Hijacking) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

answer.headline: Gathered 4 record(s) from 2 source(s); 3 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: CAPEC-593 (Session Hijacking) maps to ATT&CK techniques T1185 (Browser Session Hijacking), T1550.001 (Application Access Token), and T1563 (Remote Service Session Hijacking). Mitigations for T1185 include User Account Management (M1018) and User Training (M1017). T1563 is mitigated by Disable or Remove Feature or Program (M1042), Privileged Account Management (M1026), User Account Management (M1018), Password Policies (M1027), and Network Segmentation (M1030). T1550.001 is mitigated by Encrypt Sensitive Information (M1041), Account Use Policies (M1036), Audit (M1047), Application Developer Guidance (M1013), and Restrict Web-Based Content (M1021).
